message.abstract: <jats:p>We derive an explicit characterization of the continuous bias of diffusion operators on a closed Riemannian submanifold under a uniform sampling density. By establishing an asymptotic expansion of the associated kernel operator up to order $\varepsilon^4$, we obtain a refined description of the leading-order bias of the corresponding generator of the diffusion operator. The analysis reveals that the leading bias can be decomposed into intrinsic and extrinsic components. The intrinsic component depends on the normalized radial moments of the kernel function, the curvature of the manifold, and the target function, while the extrinsic component is determined by the kernel moments, the second fundamental form of the embedding and its derivatives, and the target function. This provides a theoretical framework for characterizing approximation errors in diffusion operators. In particular, the expansion explicitly captures the contribution arising from the discrepancy between intrinsic geodesic distance and the ambient Euclidean distance.As consequences of the bias expansion, we derive a moment-basedcriterion for comparing upper bounds on the leading bias induced bydifferent kernel profiles. We also obtain simplified expressions forthe intrinsic bias on manifolds of constant sectional curvature andfor the extrinsic bias of standard sphere embeddings. Numericalexperiments on circular and spherical benchmark datasets agree withthe predicted leading-order behavior. Across the tested bandwidthregimes, the compactly supported mollification kernel exhibits smallerspectral errors and better preserves eigenspace multiplicities thanthe comparison kernel, consistently with the proposed moment-basedbias criterion.</jats:p>
title: Intrinsic and Extrinsic Bias of Diffusion Operators: Asymptotic Expansion and Kernel-Dependent Comparison
